comments.content: `DocumentService.get_doc_ids_by_doc_names()` returns `None` when no document name matches (see `if not doc_ids: return` in document_service.py). Previously the list comprehension always produced a list (possibly `[None]`), so callers that only pass `doc_ids` worked. Now, when `doc_names` is absent/unmatched but `doc_ids` is provided, `doc_id not in doc_ids` raises `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable`, which is caught by the outer `except` and turned into a server error — breaking the doc_ids-only deletion path. Normalize to a list.

Also, since the whole point of the change was to avoid per-row deletes, mentioning that residual per-index queries remain is a valid improvement note. Also could mention that iteration should instead be done properly. But careful: is `user_canvas_version[i]` really a query? Peewee `ModelSelect.__getitem__` with an int returns `self.limit(1).offset(i).get()`? Actually `BaseModelSelect.__getitem__` with an int: `return self._clone().limit(1).offset(idx).get()`? ```python

Yes — it's a separate query per index, and `.get()` raises DoesNotExist if out of range (caught by except DoesNotExist → returns None). So one query per version beyond 20. Pre-existing but in the changed block. I'll flag as medium performance.

comments.content: The lookup filters only on `Document.name`, with no `tenant_id`/`kb_id` scoping. Since `document_rm()` authenticates with an API token but never checks that the resolved documents belong to that token's tenant, this bulk variant now resolves (and deletes) every document with a matching name across all tenants — whereas the previous single-name helper only hit the first match. Consider joining `Knowledgebase` and filtering on the caller's tenant (or validating ownership in the caller) before passing these ids to the delete path.

comments.content: The ids handed to `get_by_ids()` were resolved by document *name* only (`DocumentService.get_doc_ids_by_doc_names()` filters on `cls.model.name.in_(...)` with no tenant/KB restriction), and `get_by_ids()` likewise filters only on `id`. So `doc_dic` can contain documents that belong to other tenants. Since the removal loop then uses each document's own `tenant_id` (line 646) for `remove_document()`/`STORAGE_IMPL.rm()`, a caller holding any valid API key can now delete *every* document with a matching name in *every* tenant — the old per-name lookup only touched the first match, so this change materially widens a cross-tenant data-loss path. Restrict the fetched/deleted docs to the API key's tenant before adding them to `doc_dic` (preferably by joining `Knowledgebase.tenant_id` in the service query, e.g. `get_doc_ids_by_doc_names(doc_names, tenant_id)`).
